Subject: Opsify hosted eval — quickstart, endpoints & rateband asks

Hi Jared,

Thanks again for the time today — great walkthrough of Opsify's prompt orchestration use cases. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Takeaway: you and the team are leaning toward a hosted evaluation to validate latency, cost, and integration effort. We agreed hosted is the fastest path to iterate on prompt logic and measure token economics.
- Info we need to provision a proper trial: expected steady-state RPS, expected peak bursts, average/peak token lengths (input + output), any data residency or SOC2 evidence needs, and the procurement contact for a short trial agreement.
- What we'll provide: sandbox endpoints, short-lived API keys, an Opsify-specific quickstart checklist, and a conservative trial quote. Attachments: ops_quickstart-checklist.pdf (steps + required config) and opsify-eval-quote.xlsx (trial pricing bands).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Please confirm you want the hosted pilot and share the numbers above (steady/peak qps, tokens, any compliance flags).
2) Loop in procurement (if not already) — we'll send a trial quote and a one-page MSA addendum for the evaluation.
3) Kickoff: I can schedule a 30–45m technical kickoff with Camila for Wed Apr 7 at 10:00 AM PT if that works.

If you want to explore Dedicated or Private later, we can scope that in parallel, but for speed we recommend starting with hosted.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi —

Appreciate the summary and the artifacts. Confirming: yes, we want to start with a hosted evaluation. Details from our side: 
- Steady-state: ~50 requests/sec (we expect many small user interactions)
- Peak bursts: up to ~200 req/s for ~5–15 minute bursts (spikes around batch jobs)
- Average token payload: ~120 tokens total (prompt + expected completion); occasional larger runs up to ~800 tokens for long-form summaries
- Context window required: up to 2048 tokens (we may test longer later)
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence is required for procurement review but no special on-prem requirement at demo stage

Procurement contact: procurement@opsify.com (I've cc'd them). They will need the trial quote and the one-page MSA addendum.

Two quick questions: can you guarantee sandbox endpoints with a temporary rate raise during onboarding? And what are the default per-endpoint rate limits, throttling behavior, and how do you handle queued requests during bursts?

Also please send the API key for sandbox and any example curl/postman steps. Happy to do Wed Apr 7 10:00 AM PT for the technical kickoff — that works for the engineering team.

Thanks,
Jared Bloom
Head of AI Ops | Opsify
jared.bloom@opsify.ai

Hey Jared — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Quick answers and what we'll provision for the hosted pilot: 

1) Sandbox endpoints and keys
- We'll spin up a sandbox tenant for Opsify at: https://sandbox.opsify.redwood.ai (this is a test DNS that maps to an isolated slice)
- You'll get two API keys: OPSIFY-SBX-{short} (short-lived, renew on 7 days) and an Opsify admin key for config-only access.

2) Rate limits & burst behavior
- Default per-tenant baseline we can provision: 100 req/s (sustained) with burst headroom to 250 req/s for short windows (5–15 min) during onboarding.
- If you need 200 req/s sustained during trial we can provision a higher slice (we'll note cost delta in the quote).
- Throttling: we use token-bucket shaping per endpoint. When you exceed the slice, requests will receive 429 with a Retry-After; for controlled bursts we can enable queuing up to 500 inflight requests for the sandbox (not enabled on production by default).

3) Endpoint mapping + best practices
- /v1/chat -> conversational flows (streaming supported)
- /v1/completions -> single-turn generation (batch-friendly)
- Our SDK supports prefix caching and KV-cache reuse — for recommendation flows we recommend enabling prefix caching to reduce token cost.

4) Token limits and model selection
- We'll provision models that support 2048 context; for the large summarization tests we can run a higher-context variant (cost & latency tradeoffs noted in the attached quote).

5) Quickstart materials and what we need from you
- Attached: ops_quickstart-checklist.pdf (contains sample curl requests, configuration toggles, and test prompt sets).
- Please share a short traffic sample (CSV of timestamps + tokens or a few representative logs) so we can tune batching and recommend a starting slice.

Links & attachments:
- Quickstart guide in the Drive: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/drive/folders/opsify-quickstart
- Trial quote attached: opsify-eval-quote.xlsx

I'll prepare the sandbox and post the keys into a secure link once procurement signs the eval addendum. Rishi — if you want, I can run the kickoff session and walk Opsify engineering through the curl examples and the rateband knobs.

—Camila
